title: Introduce compact presubmit guard and dependency metadata index
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: Adds a lightweight presubmit guard that skips expensive integration and runtime tests for trivial churn (docs, lockfile bumps, README tweaks) and introduces a dependency metadata index used by CI to make safer dependency-update decisions. No runtime behavior changes. Expected CI median wall-clock improvement for small PRs: ~40%.
body:
Motivation: our presubmit lanes run expensive integrational checks for many PRs that only touch docs, vendor metadata, or lockfile updates. This inflates queue times and developer feedback latency. This PR introduces a compact presubmit guard that computes a small change signature and consults a dependency metadata index to decide if the full integration lane is required. The index encodes package->impact heuristics (runtime vs dev-only, critical paths, known flake-prone updates).

What this PR does: 1) tools/ci/presubmit_guard.py: new guard that inspects changed paths, git diff hunks, and a cached dependency metadata index to return a preflight verdict (skip, run-quick, run-full). 2) tools/ci/dep_indexer.py: builds dependency metadata from lockfiles, module manifests, and a small heuristics config (maintainable YAML). 3) .github/workflows/presubmit.yml: wiring to run the guard as the first step; if verdict==skip it posts a status and short-circuits heavy jobs. 4) scripts/ci_checkpoint_wrap.sh and pkg/infra/checkpoint/*: lightweight checkpoint wrappers used by CI to mark progress and mitigate orphaned runner timeouts. 5) tests/presubmit/*: unit and integration tests exercising guard logic and indexer behavior. 6) docs/ci/README.md: operational notes and how to update the dependency metadata.

Checklist: - [x] Add guard and indexer code with unit tests - [x] Integrate guard into presubmit workflow - [x] Add docs and update on-call playbook - [x] Run canary on staging CI and measure wall-clock improvements - [x] Add telemetry counters for skip/run decisions

Safety and rollout: default behaviour is conservative: the index starts with conservative heuristics and any unknowns result in run-full. We deployed this behind a feature flag for 72h on staging, observed ~37-43% median improvement for small PRs (<50 LOC, docs-only), and no missed regressions in the canary set (100 PRs sampled). We also implemented an automatic fallback: if the guard binary exits non-zero or the index is unavailable, workflow falls back to run-full to avoid silent skips.

Operational notes: updating the dependency metadata is a manual step (tools/ci/dep_indexer.py --update) that will later be automated from nightly lockfile scans. The docs directory includes a CONTRIBUTING section describing signals to mark a package as dev-only or low-impact.

Related: ENG-452 introduces the initial heuristics schema; SUP-210 was an incident where an infra-only bump triggered a long presubmit and contributed to release delay.

CI summary: first run had one flaky test in tests/presubmit/test_guard.py that was fixed in a follow-up commit (deterministic tempdir timing). Final CI: all checks passed.

Merge: squash merge to main.
